category: routed public IPv4 and IPv6 over WireGuard

free_tier.stated: No free tier; the product is quote-only: "Request a quote" and "We review every tunnel order individually."

egress.terms: "Ordinary traffic is unlimited and not metered per GB. Each tunnel has a monthly reference level: 1 TB for every full euro of the monthly price excluding VAT, rounded up, at least 3 TB." Above that: "Going above the level is not a breach and costs nothing by itself" and the vendor says it will not cut a tunnel for volume alone.; ingress: tcp+udp
egress.free_allowance: "Ordinary traffic is unlimited and not metered per GB. Each tunnel has a monthly reference level: 1 TB for every full euro of the monthly price excluding VAT, rounded up, at least 3 TB." Above that: "Going above the level is not a breach and costs nothing by itself" and the vendor says it will not cut a tunnel for volume alone.

interface_detail: Quote and ticket flow, then a client-configured tunnel; no API named.
tooling: wg-quick on MikroTik, OPNsense, pfSense, Linux or a VM
chaining: The routed prefix plus a free-tier VM gives a whole subnet rather than one forwarded port range.

limits.value: 1 TB per full euro of monthly price, minimum 3 TB
one active WireGuard peer per tunnel; single endpoint, no SLA

binding_note: The reference level is the only counter, and it is generous by construction: at a 3 EUR monthly price the level is 3 TB, which is 2.728 TiB, so 1 TiB/month sits at a third of the allowance. The binding constraint is really the quote and the one-peer shape.

identity_cost.detail: A quote request through the support system followed by payment; activation is human: "Activation normally takes one to five business days from the later of payment and receipt of your key." The account form was not read.

reliability_note: Single endpoint, best effort, no SLA by default; a second endpoint is a paid add-on. Outbound 25 is closed until reviewed.
confidence_note: The routing shape, the protocol, the fair-use formula and the process are all first-party. The price itself is quote-only, so cost per TiB stays unverified.

evidence.proved: WireGuard over UDP, a /32 or larger IPv4 block routed for a user, an IPv6 prefix, all ports forwarded, monthly reference level of 1 TB per euro with a 3 TB floor, one peer per tunnel, no BGP needed
a complete wg-quick configuration example with the client-supplied private key and the vendor's endpoint
outbound TCP 25 closed by default and opened after review; addresses are the vendor's PA space

price_per_tb_month: quote only; the volume reference level is 1 TB per full euro of monthly price with a 3 TB minimum
notes: The only provider that states a volume policy in a formula a reader can apply, and the only one that says outright it will not cut a tunnel for volume. WireGuard only: "WireGuard only. Other protocols are not offered." No price is published, so this row establishes shape and volume policy rather than cost.

extras.wg_detail: The vendor publishes the exact wg-quick shape it expects, with keys exchanged by ticket: "You send us your WireGuard public key in a ticket. We reply with our endpoint, our public key, your addresses and the gateway addresses." The published block is a standard [Interface]/[Peer] pair with AllowedIPs 0.0.0.0/0.

Each tunnel has a monthly reference level: 1 TB for every full euro of the monthly price excluding VAT, rounded up, at least 3 TB." Above that: "Going above the level is not a breach and costs nothing by itself" and the vendor says it will not cut a tunnel for volume alone.
extras.transit_note: NovaNode PA space registered in Luxembourg and routed statically to the tunnel.
